breakdown.description: Biot number assesses temperature gradients inside the solid (internal conduction vs external convection), not whether the surrounding fluid temperature is uniform.
breakdown.reason: The agent correctly identified that the Biot number assesses the temperature uniformity within the solid, not the fluid. The generated prompt asks to "determine if the temperature within the steel sphere can be considered uniform," which directly corrects the original error and aligns with the ground truth's focus on the "SOLID temperature".

breakdown.description: Using fluid properties (or interpreting Bi as a fluid-uniformity metric) misapplies the Biot number concept.
breakdown.reason: The agent correctly reframed the application of the Biot number. Instead of incorrectly linking it to fluid uniformity, the generated prompt correctly links the Biot number analysis to the decision of whether the lumped capacitance method can be used, which is the standard application of this concept, as reflected in the ground truth.
